statements.quote: I wrote earlier this year about my prediction that ADA will be brought to bear in the fight for accessible mental health care. ... GAME ON, people. GAME ON.
statements.context: Health policy update on the DOJ's first ADA settlement resolving employment discrimination based on alcohol use disorder. The author restates his earlier 2023 prediction (from his Perez v. Sturgis article) that the Americans with Disabilities Act will be used as an enforcement tool for access to mental health care.
statements.post_title: Alcohol Use Disorder is a Disability According to the US DOJ: Mental Health Parity is Joined by ADA Enforcement?
statements.finder_note: Restatement of an earlier call; the post treats the DOJ settlement as supporting evidence.

statements.quote: So if alcohol use disorder is a disability…and it is an ADA violation to discriminate, it follows that reasonable accommodations are also due to those with alcohol use disorder…and it might follow other psychiatric disabilities.
statements.context: After quoting the DOJ settlement (alcohol use disorder is an ADA-covered disability), the author infers that reasonable accommodations are due for AUD and might extend to other psychiatric disabilities. He then applies this to payer 'fail first' policies (NQTLs) and access to SAINT neuromodulation.
statements.post_title: Alcohol Use Disorder is a Disability According to the US DOJ: Mental Health Parity is Joined by ADA Enforcement?
statements.finder_note: Conditional legal inference; anticipates ADA accommodation claims extending to psychiatric disabilities and payer policies.

statements.quote: We will all survive without private equity investors.
statements.context: Discussing 70,000 Kaiser nurses on strike and UK doctors' strikes, the author predicts society will survive without private equity investors in health care, in contrast to the consequences of losing doctors and nurses.
statements.post_title: "I Am Determined to Prove A Villain" is Great Theater and Bad Health Care Policy
statements.finder_note: Rhetorical contrast asserting private equity is dispensable to health care.

statements.quote: Very few of us will survive the kinds of predictable causes of early death that will commonly befall us if we let all the doctors and nurses quit.
statements.context: Conditional warning: if doctors and nurses are allowed to quit en masse (strikes, burnout, private equity), predictable causes of early death (appendicitis, accidents, infections, psychiatric emergencies) will kill many people.
statements.post_title: "I Am Determined to Prove A Villain" is Great Theater and Bad Health Care Policy
statements.finder_note: Conditional ('if we let all the doctors and nurses quit'); extreme framing.

statements.quote: This is the beginning of a remarkable change in the treatment of psychiatric disorders.
statements.context: Post celebrating Medicare NTAP (new technology add-on payment) approval for SAINT (Stanford Accelerated Intelligent Neuromodulation Treatment) in the inpatient setting and AMA category III CPT codes for outpatient use. The author predicts these payment pathways mark the start of a remarkable change in psychiatric treatment.
statements.post_title: NTAP Means SAINT Treatment for Depression can be Paid By Medicare in the Hospital
statements.finder_note: Author is a SAINT provider (Fermata) and advocated for the NTAP; own-interest claim.

statements.quote: It opens the door for every breakthrough treatment to get additional payment models in the future. To be very clear, this is how psychedelic medicine will be paid for.
statements.context: The author claims the NTAP precedent for SAINT opens the door for other breakthrough treatments to get add-on payment models, and states that psychedelic medicine will be paid for through the same Medicare payment mechanism.
statements.post_title: NTAP Means SAINT Treatment for Depression can be Paid By Medicare in the Hospital
statements.finder_note: Compound: general claim about breakthrough treatments plus a specific call on how psychedelic medicine will be reimbursed.

statements.quote: let’s keep advocating for coverage in EVERY setting, not just hospitals. It’s a huge leap forward. More are coming….
statements.context: Close of the NTAP post. After urging advocacy for SAINT coverage in every setting, not just hospitals, the author says more coverage advances are coming.
statements.post_title: NTAP Means SAINT Treatment for Depression can be Paid By Medicare in the Hospital
statements.finder_note: Vague; 'More are coming' refers to further payment or coverage advances for rapid-acting treatments.

statements.quote: My friend Dave Chase has been writing about the coming apocalypse in liability for corporate America for a while ... I’m not a lawyer. But I can see the writing on the wall…and write about it.
statements.context: ERISA section of the daily-writing essay. The author restates Dave Chase's forecast of a coming liability apocalypse for corporate America from ERISA fiduciary lawsuits, citing lawyer Jerry Schlichter (2-0 at the Supreme Court, $600M+ retirement settlements) now targeting healthcare plans at firms such as Anthem, Target, T-Mobile, Walgreens and Lockheed Martin. The author endorses it: he can see the writing on the wall.
statements.post_title: Writing Every Day: You Won't Read it All, Which Is The Point.
statements.confidence_phrase: I can see the writing on the wall
statements.finder_note: Endorsed restatement of Dave Chase's third-party forecast; the Schlichter target list is quoted from Chase, not the author.

statements.quote: Alternatively, you can have class action lawyers and federal regulators dismantle the next decade of your fortune.
statements.context: Closing the ERISA section, the author addresses wealthy corporate decision-makers: either change health coverage to include mental health benefits that help people with psychiatric illness, or face class action lawyers and federal regulators dismantling the next decade of their fortune. Conditional call on ERISA fiduciary liability enforcement.
statements.post_title: Writing Every Day: You Won't Read it All, Which Is The Point.
statements.finder_note: Conditional and rhetorical (offered as a choice); implies ERISA class actions and federal enforcement against employer health plans over the next decade.

statements.quote: This is also going to be a huge pain in the neck for individuals working in those settings, because more suicides will be a big deal. ... Honestly, I hope the numbers are as sobering as I fear they will be.
statements.context: Author's expectation about the effect of The Joint Commission's 2024 sentinel-event rule on staff in inpatient, emergency, residential and intensive outpatient settings: more post-discharge suicides will count and be scrutinized.
statements.post_title: I Was Today Years Old When Suicide Became a Sentinel Event*
statements.finder_note: Implied horizon is 2024 when the rule takes effect.

statements.quote: However, making it something we have to follow up on, something we have to report on, and some hospitals are graded on, and audited for brings an entire new level of seriousness to post-discharge suicide and its follow up.
statements.context: Author's claim that mandatory reporting, grading and auditing under the 2024 Joint Commission sentinel-event rule will raise the seriousness with which hospitals treat post-discharge suicide and follow-up.
statements.post_title: I Was Today Years Old When Suicide Became a Sentinel Event*
statements.finder_note: Present-tense assertion about a consequence of a rule that has not yet taken effect; borderline.

statements.quote: Honestly, I hope the numbers are as sobering as I fear they will be. And I hope they push us towards more effective treatments, like SAINT neuromodulation , Esketamine, and other rapid-acting therapeutics.
statements.context: Author expects that once post-discharge suicides are counted as sentinel events from 2024, the counts will be sobering (high), and hopes this pushes the field toward SAINT neuromodulation, esketamine and other rapid-acting treatments.
statements.post_title: I Was Today Years Old When Suicide Became a Sentinel Event*
statements.finder_note: Compound: a fear-based expectation about the counted numbers plus a hope about treatment adoption. The hope has no predictive reading on its own.

statements.quote: There is still a lot of research to be done before these become well-established medicines. ... But this Christmas, I am hopeful we will have new and powerful treatments for depression under the tree in the near future!
statements.context: After arguing that COMP360's phase 2b TRD result (29.1% remission at week 3, p<0.002) shows a phase-3-sized difference in a phase-2-sized trial, the author tempers expectations: psilocybin-class drugs will need much more research before becoming established medicines for depression and PTSD.
statements.post_title: Mushrooms: The Original Christmas Miracle?
statements.confidence_phrase: still a lot of research to be done
statements.finder_note: Implies eventual establishment but with a substantial delay; no date.

statements.quote: Today, a new paper hit the press. And it will change what you understand to be possible.
statements.context: Post (2024-01-05) on the SHIFT trial (Stanford Hypnosis Integrated with Functional Connectivity-targeted Transcranial Stimulation; Faerman et al., Nature Mental Health, 2024; Nolan Williams senior author group) that used fMRI-guided TMS to change hypnotizability, a stable trait. The author claims the paper will change what readers understand to be possible: modifying traits, not only states, with neuromodulation.
statements.post_title: A SHIFT in The Possible: fMRI Guided Brain Stimulation Crosses a New Threshold
statements.finder_note: Rhetorical impact claim about a just-published paper; hard to resolve.

statements.quote: I’m thrilled to see that if SHIFT can’t be modified to treat my problems, Kristen Cherian, Ph.D. et al.’s remarkable work with magnesium-ibogaine might be the kind of broad spectrum and potent healing we all hope for access to, in the context of both psychiatric illness and traumatic brain injury
statements.context: Commenting on Cherian et al. (Nature Medicine, Jan 2024) on magnesium-ibogaine in special operations veterans with TBI, where the author says disability, trauma, depression and anxiety all resolved in historically hard-to-treat cases, he suggests magnesium-ibogaine might be a broad-spectrum, potent healing therapy that people will gain access to for psychiatric illness and TBI.
statements.post_title: A SHIFT in The Possible: fMRI Guided Brain Stimulation Crosses a New Threshold
statements.finder_note: Hedged potential-and-hope statement about a therapy's future role and access; no date.

statements.quote: I will highlight a few of the technologies that I see as plausibly useful on the horizon for healing the minds and hearts of individuals injured by trauma:
statements.context: After documenting PTSD rates in ICU survivors (about 20%) and ICU staff (up to 73% after COVID-19), the author lists technologies he sees as plausibly useful on the horizon for trauma: magnesium-ibogaine, MDMA (submitted to the FDA for PTSD by Lykos Therapeutics), COMP360 (Phase IIb data for PTSD), Nightware, the PRISM EEG neurofeedback system from GreyMatters Health, EMDR, and GammaCore (submitted for FDA breakthrough status for PTSD). He closes: 'The options are increasing. We need them.'
statements.post_title: The ICU is Traumatic For Everyone
statements.finder_note: Umbrella call over seven PTSD technologies. The MDMA/Lykos FDA submission and the GammaCore breakthrough request are stated as facts with no explicit approval call.

statements.quote: Psilocybin analog COMP360 has Phase IIb safety data announced—with more data coming—for PTSD.
statements.context: Item in the list of trauma technologies the author sees as 'plausibly useful on the horizon'. COMP360, a psilocybin analog, has Phase IIb safety data for PTSD announced, and the author says more data are coming.
statements.post_title: The ICU is Traumatic For Everyone
statements.finder_note: Expects further COMP360 PTSD data; no date given and the sponsor is not named in the text.

statements.quote: We have hope on the horizon. Psychedelic medicines like LSD have promising early clinical data and more coming in GAD (pre-print from my group).
statements.context: Closing section of a post on benzodiazepines and suicide risk. The author says better anxiety treatments are needed and expects more clinical data on LSD for generalized anxiety disorder (GAD), citing a pre-print from his own research group.
statements.post_title: Benzos (benzodiazepines) Are Associated With Death By Suicide.
statements.finder_note: Vague; expects more LSD-in-GAD clinical data. Author's own group (control candidate).

statements.quote: Pre-prints may be a bit of a jailbreak? We shall see.

statements.post_title: Get the Word Out: Preprints, Peer-Review, and It's Discontents
statements.finder_note: Vague, phrased as a question with 'We shall see'; no concrete outcome.

statements.quote: It was heavy on my face after 30 min, as was some neck strain. This will make it not a productivity tool unless you are in the “neck workout set.”

A class action alleges Johnson & Johnson's Pension & Benefits Committee breached ERISA fiduciary duty by letting its PBM charge $10,239.69 for a generic drug available for about $40. The author says thousands of similar ERISA fiduciary cases are coming. '4' is a footnote marker defining 'gravamen'.

statements.post_title: Lawsuits for Health Plan Scams Have Begun!

statements.post_title: Lawsuits for Health Plan Scams Have Begun!

statements.post_title: Lawsuits for Health Plan Scams Have Begun!
statements.finder_note: Litigation-volume call about employers suing plan administrators for data.

'It' = GLP-1 medication as a way to reduce child sexual abuse risk in people with pedophilic urges. Preceded by 'This will be an open question.' and followed by 'People could request the treatment without having to scream, I am a pedophile.'

statements.finder_note: Speculative; hedged with 'Perhaps'. Concerns a possible future clinical use, not a trial readout.

'This impracticality' = traditional TMS requiring 36 once-daily visits because insurers pay once a day, which depressed patients with pathological indecision cannot manage. The author predicts business models built on 36-day TMS will not work.

statements.finder_note: General prediction about TMS clinic business models; the author is founder of Fermata, a competing interventional psychiatry practice.
